question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the Pythagorean identity 

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x=1.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic Pythagorean identity

$$
{cosh}^{2}⁡x-{sinh}^{2}⁡x=1.
$$

Using the above, we rewrite the denominator and calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({cosh}^{3}⁡x-{sinh}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int \operatorname{cosh}⁡x({cosh}^{2}⁡x-{sinh}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \operatorname{cosh}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sinh}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$
